descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration, which has held the presidency since 1861
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that has held a majority in both houses of Congress since the 1878 elections

compile_desc.R: the party that has held the presidency since 1861
compile_desc.D: the party that has held a majority in both houses of Congress since the 1878 elections

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Greenback-Labor and a Prohibition nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Garfield, Hancock, Arthur, English, Weaver, Hayes, Grant, Blaine, Sherman, Conkling or Tilden

slice_sources.men: 1880 census (Tenth Census); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1880 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1880 census (Tenth Census); women 21+ outside the South; no state let women vote for president in 1880 (women voted in Wyoming Territory, which had no electoral votes), so this slice casts no presidential vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1880 census (Tenth Census); white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1880 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1880 census (Tenth Census); Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; Black men still voted in large numbers after Reconstruction, but violence, fraud and ballot-box laws already cut their turnout; the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1880 census (Tenth Census); foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.
